concepts.name: Panchayati Raj: philosophy, committees, Gram Sabha, tiers and elections
concepts.description: Gandhian basis of Panchayati Raj, the committees from Balwant Rai Mehta to Gadgil, and the Gram Sabha, three-tier and election scheme of the 73rd Amendment.
concepts.idea: Panchayati Raj grew from successive committees into the constitutional Gram Sabha-based three-tier scheme of Part IX.
concepts.rule: Balwant Rai Mehta (1957) proposed three tiers with the Samiti executive, the Zila Parishad advisory and the Collector as chairman; Ashok Mehta (1977) proposed two tiers with the Zila Parishad executive; G.V.K. Rao proposed a District Development Commissioner; Singhvi sought constitutional status and tribunals; Thungon made the Collector CEO; Gadgil recommended an SFC and SEC. The Gram Sabha (Art 243A) is all registered voters of the village. Art 243B gives three tiers, intermediate optional for a State not exceeding 20 lakh. Members are directly elected; intermediate and district chairpersons indirectly; the village chairperson as State law decides.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Ashok Mehta Committee (1977):

1. It recommended that a minister for Panchayati Raj be appointed in the State council of ministers.
2. It recommended that the Election Commission of India itself conduct Panchayat elections.
3. It recommended that Panchayati Raj bodies be kept away from taxation and be funded through State grants.
4. It recommended that elections after a supersession be held within one year.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: a minister for Panchayati Raj in the State council of ministers was among its recommendations. Statement 2 is incorrect: it suggested that the State's chief electoral officer, in consultation with the Chief Election Commissioner, organise the polls. Statement 3 is incorrect: it wanted Panchayati Raj bodies to have compulsory powers of taxation to mobilise their own resources. Statement 4 is incorrect: the period proposed was six months. Hence the answer is 1 only.
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect
'4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct

concepts.name: 73rd Amendment: reservation, tenure, finance, safeguards and agriculture items of the Eleventh Schedule
concepts.description: Articles 243D-243O: reservation, tenure, disqualification, powers, finance, SFC, SEC, exemptions, transition and court bar; election scheme; agriculture items of the Eleventh Schedule.
concepts.idea: Part IX fixes reservation, a five-year term, State-law finance and election safeguards, while devolution under the Eleventh Schedule stays at State discretion.
concepts.rule: Art 243D reserves SC/ST seats in proportion to population in the Panchayat area and not less than one-third for women including SC/ST women; Backward Class reservation is optional. Panchayats last five years from the first meeting, with fresh election within six months unless under six months remain. Min age 21. 243G is enabling; 243H authorises taxes; 243I SFC every five years; 243K SEC appointed by Governor; 243M exempts Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Scheduled/Tribal Areas; 243O bars courts. The Eleventh Schedule has 29 items.

questions.q: A Panchayat has 24 seats, of which 2 are reserved for SC women and 1 for ST women as part of the SC/ST quota. Under Article 243D, what is the least number of further seats (outside the SC and ST quota) that must be reserved for women?
questions.e: Not less than one-third of all seats (8 of 24) go to women, and this counts the 3 SC/ST women seats; so at least 5 more are needed.
w: 8 ignores that SC/ST women seats count toward the one-third.

A fresh election must be held within six months and the new Panchayat serves the remaining four months

questions.e: If the remainder of the term is under six months no election is needed; otherwise elections are held within six months and the new body serves only the balance.
w: A reconstituted body never gets a fresh full term.
Election is not required when under six months remain.
No one-year period exists in the Article.
